steps.title: Klaviyo: AI Email Marketing & SMS | B2C CRM
Klaviyo: Sign Up for Free Today
steps.note: Stopped: account form or bot check reached.

jtbd_fit.evidence: Subhead: "Composer turns customer data into revenue. You approve the plan, and every result is measured."

capability_visible.evidence: Hero shows product UI with a revenue summary and an AI recommendations panel.

pricing_transparency.evidence: Pricing is a nav link only in captured steps.

time_to_value.evidence: Flow stopped at the signup form.

friction.evidence: Signup is one email field or Google, nothing else (step 2).

trust.evidence: Named brands (Funko, Dollar Shave Club, Glossier, Dermalogica) and a customer count.

mobile.evidence: Mobile capture exists for step 1 but was not assessed.

states.evidence: No error or empty states reached.

value_prop_clarity.evidence: Two category labels compete: "The autonomous B2C CRM" eyebrow and "AI marketing agent" headline.

proof_quality.evidence: "Powering 200,000+ relationship-driven brands across 100 countries" is unsourced; dashboard figures look like demo data and are not labelled as such.

persuasion_integrity.evidence: "You approve the plan" frames AI as supervised, not magic.

cta_logic.evidence: "Sign up" and "Sign up with Google" are clear. A promo banner ("Try it now") competes for the click.

read.summary: A product-led pitch with the lightest signup of the three pilots. The AI-agent framing is current, but category labels compete.
pros: Signup asks for one email or Google, the lowest friction here.
Hero shows real product UI and a concrete recommendation.
"You approve the plan" addresses fear of an autonomous agent.
cons: Eyebrow and headline describe the product in two different ways.
Demo dashboard numbers are not labelled as sample data.
A promo banner adds a second competing CTA.
read.howItSells: Sells outcome (revenue) with supervised automation, supported by well-known DTC brands and scale. The AI framing is the hook; the proof is the logo bar.
copy: Say what the human still controls.
avoid: Two competing category names in the hero.
unknowns: What the first-run experience asks next.
Whether "Composer" is available on the free plan.

hypothesis.statement: Labelling the hero dashboard as sample data and removing the promo banner will increase trust and signup completion.
hypothesis.guardrail: Banner-driven feature awareness (click rate on the announcement)
hypothesis.decisionRule: Ship if completion rises and the announcement loses no more than an agreed share of clicks.

claims.text: Composer turns customer data into revenue
